blockers.title: The authored G16 contract drops mandatory corpus/evidence members and three shared-lane result classes
blockers.subjectEvidence: G16-1 is only a component-A example; G16-4 merely requires an undefined independent-release evidence object; G16-5 requires results only for SL-2/SL-3/SL-4. The evidence string permits 'manifest/tree/declarations/conformance report or core inventory' plus a selector decision record.
blockers.governingMeasurement: At the subject-pinned file-08 digest, live row DR-G16 requires a change-impact corpus x component/language/platform matrix, forced dependency/ownership mutations, aggregate release selection, selected-lane explanation, per-lane signed closure evidence, skipped-lane proof, and shared-core plus protocol/semantic/lock/offline/bundle results. The subject cites this file only as 'DR-121 row; DR-G16 named' and never carries or discharges the rest of the live G16 row.
blockers.counterexample: A harness can satisfy all five authored classes with one A-only selection case, any partial report path for each selected lane, and SL-2/SL-3/SL-4 results. It need never test the component/language/platform matrix, prove a skipped lane, exercise aggregate release selection, produce signed closure evidence, or record results/deferrals for SL-1, SL-5, or SL-6. That successor would pass this candidate while failing the live DR-G16 contract.
blockers.impact: This is a direct acceptance escape across DR-121 OBL-3/OBL-4/OBL-5/OBL-6 and condition-4 DR-G16, including the prompt's required attack on silent SL-5/SL-6 deletion. Naming lanes in sharedLanes does not preserve their required result evidence.
blockers.requiredRepair: Carry the live DR-G16 row or an exact obligation decomposition, then define a closed corpus/result map covering every component/language/platform selection class, selected and skipped explanations, signed per-lane closure evidence, aggregate release selection, and SL-1 through SL-6. A D-002-deferred lane may have an explicit blocked-on-ride or preview-not-required standing with its named owner; it may not disappear from the result map.

blockers.title: The selector has no authoritative change-to-component ownership relation, so all-and-only selection and fail-safe behavior are not computable
blockers.subjectEvidence: The model is three prose assertions: inputs are 'Declared component ownership and dependency metadata (manifest + index custody)', that metadata selects lanes, and ambiguity selects a 'wider set (including shared lanes that the ambiguity touches)'. No declaration shape, custody rule, changed-unit mapping, lane universe, closure algorithm, or shared-surface trigger map is defined.
blockers.governingMeasurement: The DR-121 cell requires an ownership/dependency selection model, while live DR-G16 requires all and only required lanes from declared ownership/dependencies and forbids waiver for an affected omitted lane. The accepted DR-103 manifest schema and its later v11 successor provide component dependency edges and release publisher/provenance custody, but no monorepo source-unit-to-component/shared-surface ownership map. This candidate does not add one.
blockers.counterexample: For a changed new top-level source, renamed file, shared build input, or conflicting ownership declaration, manifest/index bytes do not identify which repository lane owns the change. Because 'the ambiguity touches' is itself unknown, selecting an unspecified wider subset can still omit the affected lane; otherwise an implementation must make path filters the de facto authority despite mustNot. G16-2/G16-3 cannot prove correctness because the candidate supplies no authoritative oracle against which omitted dependency/owner cases are judged.
blockers.impact: OBL-1 is claimed answered but the load-bearing relation needed to derive the selector result is absent. The fail-safe sentence states a desired outcome without defining how to bound the possible affected set, leaving the exact under-selection failure the source prohibits.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define the vendor-neutral authoritative ownership declaration/custody model and a deterministic selection algorithm: changed-unit to owner mapping, metadata/self-change handling, deletion/rename behavior, transitive reverse-dependency closure, shared-surface triggers, and the closed lane universe. Missing/conflicting/unbounded ownership or dependency impact must either refuse or select the entire possibly affected closed universe; selected and skipped explanations must be derivable from those records. Path filters may implement a declared mapping but may not define it.

blockers.title: The proposed independent-release evidence is satisfiable by a lockstep same-version release train
blockers.subjectEvidence: The rules deny lockstep, but evidence is only a lane emission plus the selector decision that included or excluded it. G16-4 checks emission of that object; G16-5 checks SL-2/SL-3/SL-4 triggering. ID-DEP-C5 says a bundle cannot be the only route, but no authored test or evidence proves that rule.
blockers.counterexample: Give core and every component one common version, require every release to advance that version and publish in one train, then emit a selector record and the listed lane artifacts. Every authored independentRelease/G16 requirement can pass even though no component can release independently and the same-version coupling forbidden by file 02 remains intact.
blockers.governingMeasurement: File 02 says independent releases do not create lockstep versions. Live DR-G16 requires aggregate release selection. File 04's anti-lockstep section and DR-127 define the concrete hostile cases: component N+1 with unchanged supported core, core N+1 with unchanged supported components, independent rollback/coexistence, and no bundle promotion gate. The subject names DR-127 only for SL-6's route but provides none of this as OBL-6 evidence.
blockers.impact: The artifact's obligation decomposition falsely marks independent release evidence answered. A normative 'do not' with no discriminating evidence leaves hidden lockstep conforming to the candidate, which is one of the dispatch's explicit attacks.
blockers.requiredRepair: Make independent-release evidence discriminate lockstep from independence: bind independently versioned release identities and compatibility selection, require at least component-new/core-unchanged and core-new/component-unchanged selection evidence plus independent rollback/coexistence and a non-bundle route, and join aggregate-selection results into G16. Consume DR-111/DR-127 for compatibility/anti-lockstep semantics rather than minting their windows; if those owners block the evidence, mark OBL-6 explicitly conditional instead of answered.

verdictStatement: The candidate preserves the source quotations, tooling reservation, six architecture lane names, and non-authorizing posture, but it is not a complete DR-121/G16 design contract. Its G16 classes omit mandatory live-row corpus/evidence members and SL-1/SL-5/SL-6 results; its selector defines no authoritative repository-change ownership relation or computable impact closure; and its release evidence can be emitted by a lockstep same-version train. These are independently load-bearing acceptance escapes.

authorityOfThisVerdict.note: Independent measurement only. DR-121 remains OPEN; coordinator disposition is separate.
